result.title: Flow Matching for Sampled-Data Control of Angular Distributions
result.summary: Synchronization and clustering in oscillator networks depend on the joint distribution of the phases. Flow Matching can steer this distribution by learning an angular velocity field from shortest arcs between paired configurations. Each arc is traversed at constant speed, yet the resulting field can vary along its own trajectories. In this article, we study how to control angular transport on the circle and product torus when each controller evaluation selects a rate to hold until the next update. Using the same local velocity samples, Flow Matching learns the instantaneous angular rate and MeanFlow learns its average along the reference trajectory over the control interval. Under direct angular actuation, holding the exact average gives the reference displacement. We relate the displacement error of holding the instantaneous rate and the training residual of MeanFlow to the conditional covariance of the teacher velocities. Experiments with 100 phases show that endpoint pairing affects the comparison. MeanFlow gives smaller one-step errors under minibatch pairing, while permutation alignment reverses the ranking for exchangeable phase clusters.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究圆与乘积环面上相位分布（振荡子网络的同步与聚类）的角向输运控制：对比 Flow Matching 学到的瞬时角速度与 MeanFlow 学到的区间平均速度，在「每次控制评估选定速率并保持到下次更新」的采样数据设定下分析位移误差，并把误差与教师速度的条件协方差联系起来，用 100 个相位的实验比较不同端点配对方式下的排序变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「区间保持平均速度 vs 瞬时速度」的位移误差及条件协方差分析，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态按离散间隔更新、更新粒度与状态迁移保真度、以及流量类生成器的步长设计提供概念类比，可供核查，但与原论文的推理任务无直接联系。
